arxiv-2103-03842.title: Overcoming Poor Word Embeddings with Word Definitions
arxiv-2103-03842.creator: Christopher Malon
arxiv-2103-03842.description: Abstract Modern natural language understanding models depend on pretrained subword embeddings, but applications may need to reason about words that were never or rarely seen during pretraining. We show that examples that depend critically on a rarer word are more challenging for natural language inference models.

arxiv-2208-08029.title: A Context-Aware Approach for Textual Adversarial Attack through Probability Difference Guided Beam Search
arxiv-2208-08029.creator: Huijun Liu, Jie Yu, Shasha Li, Jun Ma, Bin Ji
arxiv-2208-08029.description: Abstract Textual adversarial attacks expose the vulnerabilities of text classifiers and can be used to improve their robustness. Existing context-aware methods solely consider the gold label probability and use the greedy search when searching an attack path, often limiting the attack efficiency.

arxiv-2309-03600.title: A Novel Immersed Boundary Approach for Irregular Topography with Acoustic Wave Equations
arxiv-2309-03600.creator: Edward Caunt, Rhodri Nelson, Fabio Luporini, Gerard Gorman
arxiv-2309-03600.description: Abstract Irregular terrain has a pronounced effect on the propagation of seismic and acoustic wavefields but is not straightforwardly reconciled with structured finite-difference (FD) methods used to model such phenomena. Methods currently detailed in the literature are generally limited in scope application-wise or non-trivial to apply to real-world geometries.

arxiv-2403-05302.title: Modeling Dynamic (De)Allocations of Local Memory for Translation Validation
arxiv-2403-05302.creator: Abhishek Rose, Sorav Bansal
arxiv-2403-05302.description: Abstract . End-to-End Translation Validation is the problem of verifying the executable code generated by a compiler against the corresponding input source code for a single compilation. This becomes particularly hard in the presence of dynamically-allocated local memory where addresses of local memory may be observed by the program.

arxiv-2405-11446.title: MAML-en-LLM: Model Agnostic Meta-Training of LLMs for Improved In-Context Learning
arxiv-2405-11446.creator: Sanchit Sinha, Yuguang Yue, Victor Soto, Mayank Kulkarni, Jianhua Lu, Aidong Zhang
arxiv-2405-11446.description: Abstract . Adapting large language models (LLMs) to unseen tasks with in-context training samples without fine-tuning remains an important research problem. To learn a robust LLM that adapts well to unseen tasks, multiple meta-training approaches have been proposed such as MetaICL and MetaICT, which involve meta-training pre-trained LLMs on a wide variety of diverse tasks.

arxiv-2411-12817.title: What Makes a Good Dataset for Knowledge Distillation?
arxiv-2411-12817.creator: Logan Frank, Jim Davis
arxiv-2411-12817.description: Abstract Knowledge distillation (KD) has been a popular and effective method for model compression. One important assumption of KD is that the teacher’s original dataset will also be available when training the student. However, in situations such as continual learning and distilling large models trained on company-withheld datasets, having access to the original data may not always be possible.

arxiv-2412-16560.title: On the piecewise complexity of words
arxiv-2412-16560.creator: Ph. Schnoebelen, I. Vialard
arxiv-2412-16560.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ph. Schnoebelen, I. Vialard. The piecewise complexity h ⁡ ( u ) h(u) of a word is the minimal length of subwords needed to exactly characterise u u . Its piecewise minimality index ρ ⁡ ( u ) \rho(u) is the smallest length k k such that u u is minimal among its order- k k class [ u ] k [u]_{k} in Simon’s congruence. We initiate a study of these two descriptive complexity measures.

arxiv-2505-23785.title: Meaning Is Not A Metric: Using LLMs to make cultural context legible at scale
arxiv-2505-23785.creator: Cody Kommers, Drew Hemment, Maria Antoniak, Joel Z. Leibo, Hoyt Long, Emily Robinson, Adam Sobey
arxiv-2505-23785.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Cody Kommers, Drew Hemment, Maria Antoniak, Joel Z. Leibo, Hoyt Long, Emily Robinson, Adam Sobey. This position paper argues that large language models (LLMs) can make cultural context, and therefore human meaning, legible at an unprecedented scale in AI-based sociotechnical systems. We argue that such systems have previously been unable to represent human meaning because they rely on thin descriptions (numerical representations that enforce standardization and therefore strip human activity of the cultural context which gives it meaning).

arxiv-2506-13165.title: Non-convergence and convergence of bounded solutions to semilinear wave equation with dissipative boundary condition Note: This research was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (12272297).
arxiv-2506-13165.creator: Zhe Jiao, Xiao Li
arxiv-2506-13165.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhe Jiao, Xiao Li. This paper is concerned with the long-time dynamics of semilinear wave equation subject to dissipative boundary condition. To do so, we first analyze the set of equilibria, and show it could contain infinitely many elements. Second, we show that, for some nonlinear interior sources, the wave equations have solutions that do not stabilize to any single function, while they approach a continuum of such functions.

pmc-11437099.description: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analogs are important therapeutics for type 2 diabetes and obesity. Ecnoglutide (XW003) is a novel, long-acting GLP-1 analog. pmc-11717324.creator: John Delgado, Logan Atkins, Micah Pippin, Jessan Jishu
pmc-11717324.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The VACTERL (vertebral defects, anal atresia, cardiac defects, tracheoesophageal fistula, renal anomalies, and limb abnormalities) association represents an enigmatic syndrome requiring further study. This report describes a full-term neonate born to a multiparous woman who was found, upon further examination, to have multiple congenital abnormalities, including a bicuspid aortic valve, patent foramen ovale, tracheoesophageal fistula (TEF), asymmetric crying facies, microphallus, and a single inguinal testis.

pmc-13028691.creator: Mengke Li, Hongling Li, Yuyu Shi, Yanfang Meng
pmc-13028691.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The further development of scalable fabrication for perovskite solar cells has been considerably constrained by strong process variability and the lack of a reliable real-time predictive mechanism during the thin-film formation process. Existing machine learning-based methods are incapable of capturing the inherent multi-stage kinetic characteristics and uncertainties of the perovskite crystallization process, as they rely on deterministic point prediction models and flatten time-series signals into static features, which necessitates more advanced modeling strategies.
